content.text:
`response.headers.get('set-cookie')` now returns an array of cookies again, the same shape as in 0.27.x.

**Cause:** Axios stores the cookies as an array when it reads the response. But `AxiosHeaders.normalize()` ran each header value through `normalizeValue`, which calls `String(value)` on it. That turned the array into one comma-joined string.

**Fix:** In `lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js`, `normalizeValue` now converts each item of an array to a string and keeps the array, instead of turning the whole thing into one string. `set()` already special-cased arrays in the same way, so I removed that duplicate branch and it now just calls `normalizeValue`.

**Checked:** A quick script that sets `set-cookie` to two cookies, calls `normalize(true)`, then `get('set-cookie')` now prints `['a=1', 'b=2']`. The existing `test/unit/core/AxiosHeaders.js` tests all pass (24). I didn't run the full test suite or make a real HTTP request.

`toJSON()` still joins arrays into one comma-separated string. Code that reads headers through `toJSON()` will still see a single string; code using `get()` or the header property directly gets the array.
